evidence: control.lisp:310-320: only the topic and consumer arms call (fnn-control-peer-is-owner-p socket). The request (350-361), admin (362-363), moderation (364-367) and *fnn-hybrid-control-handler* (308-309: peer invite/accept/confirm, key redecide, tls reload, bindings reload, hybrid enroll/author/revoke) arms dispatch with no credential check. control-transport.lisp fnn-control-listen: (sb-bsd-sockets:socket-bind listener path) (sb-bsd-sockets:socket-listen listener 16) (fnn-set-nonblocking ...) (fnn-chmod path #o600)
fix: Bind under a 0077 umask (or in a 0700 private directory) so the node is never wider than 0600. Gate every mutating arm, including the hybrid handler chain, on fnn-control-peer-is-owner-p the way topic and consumer already are.
reviewer: control-transport.lisp:92-99 binds and listens before fnn-chmod 0600, and nothing sets the umask (grep finds none). Only the topic and consumer arms call fnn-control-peer-is-owner-p (control.lisp:310-333). The hybrid chain, request, admin and moderation arms have no peer-UID check. Exploiting this needs a permissive umask (with the default 022 the socket gets no group or other write bit, so connect is denied) and a parent directory that others can reach, since the control path is configured. Someone must also connect during a window of a few microseconds at startup. Darwin, Linux and OpenBSD all enforce socket-file permissions, so the 'permanent gap' variant does not apply. The real weakness is defense-in-depth: the admin arms rely on the file mode alone.
scenario: The node runs with a permissive umask (000 or 002 under a service manager or shared group). Between bind/listen and chmod 0600, the socket node is connectable by another local user, and that connection waits in the backlog until the accept thread starts. Once accepted, the frame is an admin vector (for example a `peer add` or `account` change) or a peer-invite configure. It is executed because, unlike topic and consumer, these arms rely only on the file mode the race bypassed. On any platform that does not enforce socket-file permissions, the gap is permanent, not a race.
title: Admin, POST, moderation and peer/keys/tls control frames have no peer-UID check, and the socket is world-connectable between bind and chmod
